note: No house style yet. Derive it from the client's reference videos (ref-analyze) and the editor's feedback, then record it in the client's reel-profile/style.json.

reframe_sharpen.why: a 9:16 crop of a 16:9 1080p source is upscaled ~178 % and looks soft; Premiere Sharpen 15-20 and optional Noise 2-3 % hide it (client plan EP02 §2). Set amount 0 to turn off.

knobs_note: Read by `reel plan` (T4.2); builds follow the compiled plan, so run `reel plan` after a change. caption_size_px: null = the caption template's size, or a whole number 32-140 px on a 1080 px wide frame (caption lines get shorter as it grows); one reel may set global.caption_size_px in edit-decisions. captions_during_hook: hide | show (captions under the hook title; client only). hook_title_sfx: true | false (the hook title's sound). highlight_colour: brand | accent | ink | #RRGGBB (the keyword caption box in Premiere; checked for contrast against the caption text and replaced by a readable brand colour, with a warning, when too faint; After Effects captions use the brand colour for now). A reel may override hook_title_sfx and highlight_colour in edit-decisions global.

camera.why: T4.1 smooth zoom: each story punch-in eases in and out over ease_ms (bezier keys on Motion Scale/Position). 0 = hard punches; a slow_push pushes across its whole piece whatever this says. Reframes, punch-outs, jump-cut zoom masks, punches on a cut or next to another shot, and 4:5 window framing stay hard.
